findings.issue_text: canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, allowing an administrator with read-only access to all groups to create groups and pass global manage checks.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() instead of the authorization-resource ID/name, causing per-group view-members/manage-members grants to be missed and preventing authorized admins from listing group members via user search.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() instead of the authorization-resource ID/name, causing per-group view-members/manage-members grants to be missed and preventing authorized admins from listing group members via user search.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same core problem: in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), groupResource.getId() is being passed to hasPermission() instead of the proper authorization resource identifier (resource name/group id). Both comments point out that this mismatch causes per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions to not work correctly, affecting the ability to properly filter and list group members. The candidate uses slightly different terminology ('authorization-resource ID/name' vs 'resource names/underlying group ids') but describes the same fundamental bug.
